device.model: Zaber device over the ASCII serial protocol
device.name: Zaber serial axis (zaber.serial.ascii.AsciiAxis)

facts.text: The clone is a library for controlling Zaber devices over a serial port
AsciiAxis represents one axis of an ASCII device; the axis number is 1-9
AsciiAxis.send sends an AsciiCommand through the parent device and checks that the reply came from this axis
home() sends the 'home' command and then polls the axis until it is idle
move_abs(position) sends 'move abs <position>' where position is an integer in microsteps, then polls until idle
move_rel(distance) sends 'move rel <distance>' where distance is an integer number of microsteps, then polls until idle
move_vel(speed) sends 'move vel <speed>' with an integer speed and returns immediately unless blocking is true
stop() sends the 'stop' command and polls until idle; the stop command pre-empts a movement command
get_status() returns the reply device status, which is either 'BUSY' or 'IDLE'
get_position() sends 'get pos' and returns the reply data, described as the absolute position in microsteps
poll_until_idle() blocks until the device reports that the axis is idle
AsciiDevice.address is 1-99 and axis(number) returns a new AsciiAxis for an axis number of 1-9
AsciiSerial(port, ...) opens the serial port when the constructor is called
AsciiCommand.encode builds the protocol frame '/<device address> <axis number> [<message id>] <data>' terminated by CRLF

operator_required.reason: the clone states no travel range for the axis (move_abs names only integer microsteps); the site supplies the travel of the installed stage

operator_required.name: move_rel

operator_required.name: move_vel
operator_required.reason: the clone states no speed range and no unit for move_vel (it names only an integer speed); the site supplies the safe speed of the installed stage
